doc.title: Eddie Alley interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Not playing rock and roll
summary: He stuck to Lunceford, Goodman and Ellington styles and played only a couple of Beatles tunes.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Right. What was your — when your band was in existence long enough that musical styles changed a lot, did you play some rock & roll?
Not too much. I stayed with what I could really play good.
Because I was never a good rock & roll drummer or musician, so I didn’t play rock & roll. I played a couple of numbers.

Oh I played a couple of them, you know, a couple, to satisfy people. But that wasn’t my forte. I was more like Jimmie Lunceford, [inaudible] and other stuff you know and Benny Goodman stuff and Duke Ellington stuff, in that vein. Yeah.
